what_it_measures: The whole layer repeats the trial's figures within 0.01, but most of that agreement is built in: the neurons' answers are the same answers (99.6% bit for bit) and only the controls are new. What it shows is that the null is stable across seeds and at twice the size, and that the trial's 1,022 were a fair sample of the layer (7.4% against 7.3% above every control).

The only test of the neurons themselves is still the one inside the run: words picked on three questions and scored on the other three (0.68 and 0.67). A break_rel retest of the strongest is refused by census_run.py, rightly: on a shared (question, dose) cell a neuron writes its picked answer again, which this comparison measures directly. A retest needs questions no screen asked.

The lead says a neuron's push differs from a push along a random direction (unit(w_post * r), r isotropic), not that its words share a theme. A neuron's down column is a learned direction and the controls are not; a learned direction may beat an isotropic one for reasons that are the layer's, not the neuron's (its write subspace, its alignment with the unembedding). A control drawn from the layer's own columns (a random mix of them, so matched to their covariance) would ask whether the single neuron is special within what its layer writes. Such controls need no new neuron answers: the 21,504 neurons' answers stand, and 2,048 new controls are 49,152 answers, about 70 minutes.
